newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat after volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends flat after volatile trade.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates closed unchanged at 23.00 percent on Wednesday after a seesawing through the session on economic data and political factors, traders said.

"Cetes rates opened a little unnerved by a greater-then-expected hike in primary rates, coupled with early speculation the U.S. Congress would decertify Mexico" as an ally in the war against drugs, a trader said.
Primary rates on bellwether 28-day Cetes soared 201 basis points to 23.17 percent at Tuesday night's central bank auction.
The U.S. House of Representatives was expected to vote on a bill on Thursday to decertify Mexico as a drugs war ally.
U.S. Deputy Treasury Secretary Lawrence Summers said on Wednesday, in testimony to a Senate panel, that a decertification vote could harm Mexican financial markets.
Traders said a Congressional decertification resolution would upset local markets, in addition to uncertainty ahead of the forthcoming U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
"The FOMC will continue to cause instability until it meets (on March 25), on top of which there is pressure on the political front," another trader said.
"It is doubtless an element for speculation. Mexico's international image suffers and foreign investors will react quickly to the slightest move in the U.S. bond market," he added.
Yields on 30-year U.S. Treasury bonds were up to 6.87 percent in late trade, from 6.85 percent on Tuesday.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed down 40 basis points at 24.60 percent.
Dealers said that primary rates could be less volatile after the sharp gain on Tuesday night, but could trend upwards before the FOMC meeting.
"We could see more instability as the FOMC meeting draws near, although 28-day Cetes could be peaking," a money market analyst said.
Banco de Mexico drained 594 million pesos from the market by assigned a single overnight auction at 24.69 percent.
Liquidity of 2.623 million pesos was scheduled to return to the system on Thursday from prior central bank participation in the secondary market.
Traders said additional liquidity of 252 million pesos would flow into the market from an underplacement of paper at the primary auction.
